evidence: `res.json().catch(() => ({}))` turns an unparseable body into `{}`, which callers then read as data (`availability.state` undefined). Commit a8d9bc5 removes the catch, so the rejection reaches the caller's existing try/catch.
guidance_note: When writing a fetch helper, never give a parse failure a default value; let it reject to the caller's existing error path.

evidence: The hunk shows `setStatus(`...Generation failed: ${status.error}`)` writing a server string into innerHTML unescaped. The flag is a false positive: a8d9bc5 changed only the `api()` JSON-parse line, and the setStatus interpolation was there in the original PR.
guidance_note: Before writing any innerHTML template in a client script, list every interpolated value and route each one through a single escape helper, or build the node with textContent.

narrative: Round 0 flagged a silent JSON-parse fallback, and the agent fixed it correctly. Round 1 found an XSS in the status renderer, which was in the original PR and not caused by the fix. The agent fixed it by context: DOM nodes for the dropdown, one esc() for the status markup. Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: Both findings were in the original inline script and a single self-review for silent fallbacks and innerHTML sinks would have caught them, but no round was fix-caused.

evidence: The original single try wraps both `catalog.getPlayground` and `store.get` and maps any throw to 404 'playground not found', so a store failure was relabeled as a miss. 97546ff splits the try so a store failure becomes a sealed 500, and adds a test.
guidance_note: When mapping exceptions to HTTP statuses, discriminate by error type at the throwing seam rather than by which call sits inside the try.

evidence: siteHandler's `playPage` uses a bare `catch {}` that maps every getPlayground/summarize error to 404. That is the same not-found relabeling F1 named, and 97546ff did not sweep it. The agent admits the F1 fix's own getPlayground arm 'has the same latent gap' because getPlayground throws an untyped Error. Fix 4a8fd17 adds a typed PlaygroundNotFoundError at the catalog.
guidance_note: When a finding says one catch relabels failures as not-found, grep every caller of the same throwing function and fix the error's type at its source before splitting any single try.

narrative: F1 correctly found that store failures were relabeled as 404 in contentHandler. The agent fixed only that try block, leaving the untyped-error getPlayground arm and siteHandler's identical bare catch. Round 1 flagged the sibling instance. The agent then made the root fix, a typed PlaygroundNotFoundError, that should have been the first fix.
guidance_observations: The root cause, getPlayground throwing an untyped Error for not-found, was visible during the first fix; fixing at the seam in round 0 would have saved round 1.

evidence: The reviewer's case rests on 'the seed's content matches the existing file'. On a warm continue, though, the workdir file is the live conversation's working state, and the agent explains that a failed refine leaves it ahead of the store. An unconditional write would clobber what `--continue` resumes. finalizeFailure's body is not in the packet, but even on success the overwrite is at best redundant, so the guard selects which source is authoritative rather than gating a uniform operation.

`if (world.reseeded) yield ...` makes the opening progress stream one or two events. Collapsing it to one yield with a data-chosen message, as 00cdca9 does, keeps the reseed signal and makes the shape uniform.
guidance_note: When surfacing a degraded mode in a stream, vary the content of a fixed slot instead of adding a conditional extra event.

narrative: The reviewer raised two dataflow findings on the warm/cold continue path. The agent correctly pushed back on the seed-write guard: a warm workdir can legitimately be ahead of the store, so overwriting it is not harmless. It accepted the variable-yield finding with a uniform data-driven yield. Round 1 approved, and no finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: The pushback reasoned from the actual state transitions (failed refine leaves workdir ahead of store), which is the right way to test a reviewer's 'harmless overwrite' premise.

evidence: The new fork describe block's `submitToReady` is a byte-identical copy of the continue block's helper. Commit d43d79a lifts one copy to file scope and deletes both locals.
guidance_note: When a new test block needs a helper that already exists in a sibling describe, lift the helper to file scope instead of copying it.

narrative: One finding: the agent copy-pasted a test helper into the new fork block. The agent lifted it to file scope and round 1 approved. Nothing was fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Copying a helper from a neighbouring describe block is a predictable duplication; checking for reuse before writing new test scaffolding would have avoided the round.

evidence: `setNavSignedIn(session.identity)` passes the `{ subject }` object to code that sets `identEl.textContent = identity`, which renders '[object Object]'. fcf7e97 passes `.subject` instead.
guidance_note: When a client reads a server response, check the handler's response type for each field the client dereferences.

evidence: main.dev.ts copies main.ts's dataDir, port, contentPort and oauthCallbackUrl resolution verbatim. The flag is a false positive: fcf7e97 changed only the setNavSignedIn argument, and the duplication was in the original PR (the round 0 summary already noted it).
guidance_note: When creating a second entry point 'identical except X', extract the shared part first and write only X in the new file.

evidence: `.catch(() => ({ identity: null }))` turns every /session failure into 'not authenticated'. Accepting was right, but the fix in e552902 kept returning `{ identity: null }`, the same value as a real signed-out response, and that directly produced F7. The flag is a false positive: fcf7e97 did not touch this line.
guidance_note: When fixing a swallowed error, remove the fallback value as well as adding a message; if the fallback is shaped like a legitimate response, the conflation survives.

evidence: The initial `applyTheme(...)` always calls localStorage.setItem, so the change listener's `!localStorage.getItem(PREF)` guard can never pass after the first load. The flag is a false positive: e552902 touched only the session catch and the config extraction, not the theme code.
guidance_note: When writing a preference waterfall, trace each write site to confirm only an explicit user choice ever writes the storage tier.

evidence: requireSignin only un-hides #signin, so after a 401 the nav still shows the identity and signout while #create stays visible. 363b4a5 adds the full inverse of setNavSignedIn. The flag is a false positive: b5d8945 changed only the theme init line.
guidance_note: When writing a function that sets one auth state, write its inverse in the same pass and have both toggle the same element set.

evidence: The F4 fix (b5d8945) stopped the initial resolution from persisting. Its plan said the change listener's guard 'then fires correctly', but the listener itself calls `applyTheme`, so the first OS change still persisted and froze the preference. This is the same write-site bug at the second call site, a functional bug rather than a duplicated fact.
guidance_note: When fixing 'X must not write storage', grep every call of the writing function (here applyTheme) and fix each non-explicit-choice caller in the same commit.

evidence: The F3 fix e552902 surfaced the error but still returned `{ identity: null }`, so the boot code showed the signin panel on a server failure. 3e0cf87 returns `null` and guards on it, keeping the two states distinct without the reviewer's bootFailed flag.
guidance_note: When fixing a swallowed error, check whether the fallback value is indistinguishable from a legitimate response, and make the error state its own value in the same fix.

evidence: The justfile ran `tsx watch src/web/main.dev.ts` while package.json `dev` still targeted main.ts. 6b09149 points the package script at main.dev.ts and makes just delegate to it. The flag is a false positive: 3e0cf87 touched only the session catch.
guidance_note: When adding a task-runner recipe, delegate to the existing package script and change that script, rather than restating the command.

evidence: With `<html data-theme="light">` hard-coded and resolution in a body-end module script, dark-preference users see a light paint first. The flag is a false positive: the markup was in the original redesign. The fix 6b09149 copied the resolver into <head> without removing the module copy, and that duplication later cost F15 and F25.
guidance_note: When adding a pre-paint script, move the resolver there and delete the later copy instead of duplicating the logic.

evidence: `empty.textContent = ...` wiped the commons link, so the premise is true. The fix 6b09149 (`append`) left the error unstyled (F11) and next to the now-false 'No generation provider is available' copy (F17). Two follow-up rounds came from not specifying the error state's full content. The cited law has nothing to do with appending a DOM child. The flag is a false positive: 3e0cf87 did not touch this code.
guidance_note: When changing what an error panel shows, write out the panel's complete intended content for that state (label, message, styling, navigation) before choosing append versus replace.

evidence:
6b09149 appended `

`, but `.bad` is styled only under #status and #availability. Inside #empty (color: var(--muted)) the error became indistinguishable from the static text, whereas before the fix it was the panel's only text. 93c644a adds `#empty .bad`.
guidance_note: When reusing a class name in a new container, check that a CSS rule actually matches it in that container.

evidence: The signout handler did `await fetch('/session', {method:'DELETE'}); reload()` with no check for rejection or `res.ok`. f2185d5 routes the call through `api()` in a try/catch. The flag is a false positive: 93c644a was a one-line CSS change.
guidance_note: When a page already has a checked `api()` helper, use it for every request, including fire-and-forget ones like signout.

evidence: `Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8787)` gives NaN for non-numeric input, which flows into contentPort and the callback URL. That part is real. The claim that listen(NaN) silently binds a random port is not shown in the packet. The flag is a false positive: serverConfig.ts was created by e552902 (the F2 fix), but these lines moved verbatim from main.ts/main.dev.ts, so the logic predates review.
guidance_note: When parsing an env var into a number, validate it in the same expression as the parse.

evidence: f2185d5's parsePort does `if (value === undefined) return fallback;`, so the derived `port + 1` default bypasses the range check (PORT=65535 gives contentPort 65536). 1da3404 runs both sources through the check.
guidance_note: When adding a validator with a fallback parameter, route the fallback through the same check, since a derived default is as untrusted as input.

evidence: The F9 fix 6b09149 added a head resolver using `if(!t)` while the module script kept `??`. The two copies disagree on an empty-string stored value. The mismatch is real but only triggers with a corrupted or hand-edited localStorage value. The underlying problem is the duplicate resolver, which F25 later removed.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a second implementation of existing logic, make the old one consume the new one's result in the same commit.

evidence: The redesign hunk shows `<label for="provider">` removed and the select left unlabeled. da51a14 restores it. The flag is a false positive: 1da3404 changed only `??`→`||` and parsePort.
guidance_note: When rewriting markup wholesale, diff the old form's labels and aria attributes against the new markup.

evidence: The F10 fix switched `textContent=` to `append`. That kept the static 'No generation provider is available right now' copy, which is false when the fetch failed, alongside the error. The old textContent version did not show it. The cited law is a stretch for UI copy.
guidance_note: When an error state shares a container with a different state's static copy, render the error state's content explicitly instead of appending to the other state's markup.

evidence: The F13 fix wrote `n < 0`, so it accepts port 0, an ephemeral bind, while oauthCallbackUrl is built from the literal port before binding. It also advertised '0-65535'. The validation range was chosen without checking the value's consumers. The cited law is not what governs a range bound.
guidance_note: When writing a validator, derive the accepted range from every consumer of the value (here the callback URL), not from the type's nominal domain.

evidence: The shared page says 'Sign in with GitHub', but main.dev.ts wires a loopback IdP. dafd0e1 makes the copy provider-agnostic. The flag is a false positive: the copy was in the original redesign, and 83b87fd touched #empty and parsePort.
guidance_note: When adding an entry point that swaps a dependency, grep shared assets for claims about the swapped dependency.

evidence: Gate 3 justified validation as 'before the catalog grows large' while Gate 2 already seeds 100+. e40a7d0 moves the row to Gate 2 (the reviewer's option b). The flag is a false positive: the 2YEARPLAN doc was new content in this PR, and dafd0e1 only changed sign-in copy. The agent's claims about lit edges are not verifiable from the packet.
guidance_note: When writing a roadmap that orders work across gates, check each 'before X' rationale against the gate where X happens.

evidence: The Gate 3 table and the Structural Facts blocker list disagreed. The agent trimmed the table to lit's launch edges instead of growing the list, consistent with the doc's own 'lit wins' rule. The lit edge facts themselves are not in the packet. The flag is a false positive: the doc was new in this PR.
guidance_note: When a document restates a dependency list from the tracker in two places, generate both from the tracker or keep only one.

evidence: PROJECT.md's 'No product code yet' contradicts the plan's 'Gate 1 passed'. The agent repaired the stale status at its source (and in CLAUDE.md) instead of adding a precedence rule, which removes the contradiction outright. The flag is a false positive: e40a7d0 edited Gate tables, not PROJECT.md's status.
guidance_note: When a new doc declares a milestone done, grep sibling docs for status claims about that milestone and update them in the same PR.

evidence: The reviewer admits setNavSignedIn is called once per page today, and the round 5 summary said the listener does not accumulate. The finding is latent, and moving registration to init is cheap and cleaner. Listener placement is not an IO-at-the-boundary or temporal-coupling concern, so the citations are pasted. The flag is a false positive: setNavSignedIn's listener was in the original PR.
guidance_note: When writing a state-applying function, register event listeners once at init instead of inside it.

evidence: The F17 fix 83b87fd used `empty.replaceChildren(errMsg, commonsP)`, which dropped the `<span class="widget-label">` that the append version had kept. This is the third round on the same panel since F10.
guidance_note: When replacing a panel's children, start from the panel's existing structure (label, body, link) and swap only the parts that change.

evidence: The head script added for F9 duplicated the module's resolver. The reviewer's cure, having the inline script persist the resolved value, would make localStorage claim an explicit choice and break the follow-OS listener that F4 and F6 established. Deleting the module's re-resolution line is the correct single-resolver fix.
guidance_note: When adding a pre-paint script, move the resolver there and delete the later copy instead of duplicating the logic.

evidence: The F14 fix's error text 'default for TINKERPAD_CONTENT_PORT (65536)' does not tell the operator what to do, which is a real but minor defect. Failing loudly is correct, and the reviewer's clamp to `port - 1` would silently bind an undocumented port. The agent kept the failure loud and made the message actionable.
guidance_note: When a validation error can fire on a derived default, name the derivation and the env var to set in the message.

narrative: This large front-door redesign took 15 rounds. Most rounds raised fresh pre-existing issues, but 11 of 26 findings came from earlier fixes. Rounds 4, 6, 8 and 10 had only fix-caused findings. The agent generally applied the reviewer's suggested cure verbatim (append instead of textContent, setStatus plus the same sentinel, parsePort with an unchecked fallback, a duplicated head resolver), and each one spawned a follow-up. The #empty error panel alone took four rounds (F10, F11, F17, F24), and the theme resolver took four more (F4, F6, F15, F25). The late different_fix replies (F25, F26) show the agent correctly rejecting reviewer cures that would have broken behavior.
guidance_observations: Taking the reviewer's literal suggestion without specifying the full end state of the touched UI or validator caused most of the avoidable rounds; an end-state check before pushing each fix would have collapsed the #empty and parsePort chains.
Fixes that add a second copy of existing logic (the head theme script) reliably produce drift findings later; delete or consume the original in the same commit.

The PR bundled a UI redesign, a dev entry point, a justfile and a roadmap doc, so every round reviewed four scopes and kept surfacing unrelated pre-existing issues; splitting it would have kept fix-caused rounds visible and short.
